subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs be cleanup-safe by default, or should `deleteAfterRun` remain valid only for one-shot cron jobs?
rationale: This PR and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96045 encode opposite lifecycle contracts, and the choice affects persisted cron jobs, session retention, and the linked token-leak report.

options.title: Complete recurring cleanup
options.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require handling already-persisted omitted `deleteAfterRun` jobs and preserve explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

options.title: Choose one-shot-only validation
options.body: Pause or close this PR and continue through the strict-validation path after its compatibility and UI/Gateway gaps are fixed.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only default
options.body: Land this PR as a forward-only default and explicitly document that existing omitted jobs need operator action or a later migration.

recommendation.title: Complete recurring cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require handling already-persisted omitted `deleteAfterRun` jobs and preserve explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans cron defaulting, SQLite persisted-row compatibility, and product lifecycle semantics where recent history points to steipete.
